lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: expected value as a weighted average

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: From 6 items choose 2 with order mattering.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A random variable takes values 5, 4, 6 with probabilities 5/10, 2/10, 3/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
Given P(A) = 4/10 and P(B | A) = 2/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
A trial succeeds with probability 4/10 and is repeated 3 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: From 9 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 3 and arrange them in order?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A random variable takes values 19, 17, 10, 3 with probabilities 1/10, 4/10, 2/10, 3/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 1/10 and P(B | A) = 3/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
